verses.zh: （ 亞 薩 的 詩 ， 照 耶 杜 頓 的 作 法 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 ） 我 要 向 神 發 聲 呼 求 ； 我 向 　 神 發 聲 ， 他 必 留 心 聽 我 。
verses.en: For the music director, Jeduthun; a psalm of Asaph.I will cry out to God[NOTE:1] and call for help.I will cry out to God and he will pay attention[NOTE:2] to me.
notes: Psalm 77. The psalmist recalls how he suffered through a time of doubt, but tells how he found encouragement and hope as he recalled the way in which God delivered Israel at the Red Sea.
Heb “my voice to God.” The Hebrew verb קָרָא (qaraʾ, “to call out; to cry out”) should probably be understood by ellipsis (see Ps 3:4) both here and in the following (parallel) line.

verses.zh: 我 在 患 難 之 日 尋 求 主 ； 我 在 夜 間 不 住 地 舉 手 禱 告 ； 我 的 心 不 肯 受 安 慰 。
verses.en: In my time of trouble I sought[NOTE:1] the Lord.I kept my hand raised in prayer throughout the night.[NOTE:2] I[NOTE:3] refused to be comforted.
notes: The perfect with vav (ו) consecutive is best taken as future here (although some translations render this as a past tense; cf. NEB, NIV). The psalmist expresses his confidence that God will respond to his prayer. This mood of confidence seems premature (see vv. 3-4), but v. 1 probably reflects the psalmist’s attitude at the end of the prayer (see vv. 13-20). Having opened with an affirmation of confidence, he then retraces how he gained confidence during his trial (see vv. 2-12).
Here the psalmist refers back to the very recent past, when he began to pray for divine help.

Heb “my hand [at] night was extended and was not growing numb.” The verb נָגַר (nagar), which can mean “flow” in certain contexts, here has the nuance “be extended.” The imperfect form (תָפוּג, tafug, “to be numb”) is used here to describe continuous action in the past.

verses.zh: 我 想 念 神 ， 就 煩 燥 不 安 ； 我 沉 吟 悲 傷 ， 心 便 發 昏 。 （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: I said, “I will remember God while I groan;I will think about him while my strength leaves me.”[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: Or “my soul.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) with a pronominal suffix is often equivalent to a pronoun, especially in poetry (see BDB 660 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ 4.a).

verses.zh: 你 叫 我 不 能 閉 眼 ； 我 煩 亂 不 安 ， 甚 至 不 能 說 話 。
verses.en: You held my eyelids open;[NOTE:1] I was troubled and could not speak.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I will remember God and I will groan, I will reflect and my spirit will grow faint.” The first three verbs are cohortatives, the last a perfect with vav (ו) consecutive. The psalmist’s statement in v. 4 could be understood as concurrent with v. 1, or, more likely, as a quotation of what he had said earlier as he prayed to God (see v. 2). The words “I said” are supplied in the translation at the beginning of the verse to reflect this interpretation (see v. 10).

Heb “you held fast the guards of my eyes.” The “guards of the eyes” apparently refers to his eyelids. The psalmist seems to be saying that God would not bring him relief, which would have allowed him to shut his eyes and get some sleep (see v. 2).

verses.zh: 我 追 想 古 時 之 日 ， 上 古 之 年 。
verses.en: I thought about the days of old,about ancient times.[NOTE:1]
notes: The imperfect is used in the second clause to emphasize that this was an ongoing condition in the past.

verses.zh: 我 想 起 我 夜 間 的 歌 曲 ， 捫 心 自 問 ； 我 心 裡 也 仔 細 省 察 。
verses.en: I said, “During the night I will remember the song I once sang;I will think very carefully.”I tried to make sense of what was happening.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the years of antiquity.”

verses.zh: 難 道 主 要 永 遠 丟 棄 我 ， 不 再 施 恩 麼 ？
verses.en: I asked,[NOTE:1] “Will the Lord reject me forever?Will he never again show me his favor?
notes: Heb “I will remember my song in the night, with my heart I will reflect. And my spirit searched.” As in v. 4, the words of v. 6a are understood as what the psalmist said earlier. Consequently the words “I said” are supplied in the translation for clarification (see v. 10). The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) consecutive at the beginning of the final line is taken as sequential to the perfect “I thought” in v. 6.

verses.zh: 難 道 他 的 慈 愛 永 遠 窮 盡 ， 他 的 應 許 世 世 廢 棄 麼 ？
verses.en: Has his loyal love disappeared forever?Has his promise[NOTE:1] failed forever?
notes: As in vv. 4 and 6a, the words of vv. 7-9 are understood as a quotation of what the psalmist said earlier. Therefore the words “I asked” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 難 道 神 忘 記 開 恩 ， 因 發 怒 就 止 住 他 的 慈 悲 麼 ？ （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: Has God forgotten to be merciful?Has his anger stifled his compassion?” (Selah)

verses.zh: 我 便 說 ： 這 是 我 的 懦 弱 ， 但 我 要 追 念 至 高 者 顯 出 右 手 之 年 代 。
verses.en: Then I said, “I am sickened by the thoughtthat the Most High[NOTE:1] might become inactive.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “word,” which may refer here to God’s word of promise (note the reference to “loyal love” in the preceding line).
The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן, ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.

verses.zh: 我 要 提 說 耶 和 華 所 行 的 ； 我 要 記 念 你 古 時 的 奇 事 。
verses.en: I will remember the works of the Lord.Yes, I will remember the amazing things you did long ago.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And I said, ‘This is my wounding, the changing of the right hand of the Most High.’” The form חַלּוֹתִי (khalloti) appears to be a Qal infinitive construct (with a first person singular pronominal suffix) from the verbal root חָלַל (khalal, “to pierce; to wound”). The present translation assumes an emendation to חֲלוֹתִי (khaloti), a Qal infinitive construct (with a first person singular pronominal suffix) from the verbחָלָה (khalah, “be sick, weak”). The form שְׁנוֹת (shenot) is understood as a Qal infinitive construct from שָׁנָה (shanah, “to change”) rather than a plural noun form, “years” (see v. 5). “Right hand” here symbolizes by metonymy God’s power and activity. The psalmist observes that his real problem is theological in nature. His experience suggests that the sovereign Lord has abandoned him and become inactive. However, this goes against the grain of his most cherished beliefs.

verses.zh: 我 也 要 思 想 你 的 經 營 ， 默 念 你 的 作 為 。
verses.en: I will think about all you have done;I will reflect upon your deeds.”

verses.zh: 神 啊 ， 你 的 作 為 是 潔 淨 的 ； 有 何 神 大 如 神 呢 ？
verses.en: [NOTE:1] O God, your deeds are extraordinary.[NOTE:2] What god can compare to our great God?[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “yes, I will remember from old your wonders.”sn The psalmist refuses to allow skepticism to win out. God has revealed himself to his people in tangible, incontrovertible ways in the past and the psalmist vows to remember the historical record as a source of hope for the future.

Verses 13-20 are the content of the psalmist’s reflection (see vv. 11-12). As he thought about God’s work in Israel’s past, he reached the place where he could confidently cry out for God’s help (see v. 1).

Heb “O God, in holiness [is] your way.” God’s “way” here refers to his actions. “Holiness” is used here in the sense of “set apart, unique,” rather than in a moral/ethical sense. As the next line and the next verse emphasize, God’s deeds are incomparable and set him apart as the one true God.

verses.zh: 你 是 行 奇 事 的 神 ； 你 曾 在 列 邦 中 彰 顯 你 的 能 力 。
verses.en: You are the God who does amazing things;you have revealed your strength among the nations.

verses.zh: 你 曾 用 你 的 膀 臂 贖 了 你 的 民 ， 就 是 雅 各 和 約 瑟 的 子 孫 。 （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: You delivered[NOTE:1] your people by your strength[NOTE:2]—the children of Jacob and Joseph. (Selah)
notes: Heb “Who [is] a great god like God?” The rhetorical question assumes the answer, “No one!”
Or “redeemed.”

verses.zh: 神 啊 ， 諸 水 見 你 ， 一 見 就 都 驚 惶 ； 深 淵 也 都 戰 抖 。
verses.en: The waters[NOTE:1] saw you, O God,the waters saw you and trembled.[NOTE:2] Yes, the depths of the sea[NOTE:3] shook with fear.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “with [your] arm.”
The waters of the Red Sea are here personified; they are portrayed as seeing God and fearing him.
The prefixed verbal form may be taken as a preterite or as an imperfect with past progressive force.
The words “of the sea” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 雲 中 倒 出 水 來 ； 天 空 發 出 響 聲 ； 你 的 箭 也 飛 行 四 方 。
verses.en: The clouds poured down rain;[NOTE:1] the skies thundered.[NOTE:2] Yes, your arrows[NOTE:3] flashed about.
notes: The prefixed verbal form may be taken as a preterite or as an imperfect with past progressive force.
Heb “water.”
Heb “a sound the clouds gave.”

verses.zh: 你 的 雷 聲 在 旋 風 中 ； 電 光 照 亮 世 界 ； 大 地 戰 抖 震 動 。
verses.en: Your thunderous voice was heard in the wind;the lightning bolts lit up the world.The earth trembled and shook.[NOTE:1]
notes: The lightning accompanying the storm is portrayed as the Lord’s “arrows” (see v. 18).

verses.zh: 你 的 道 在 海 中 ； 你 的 路 在 大 水 中 ； 你 的 腳 蹤 無 人 知 道 。
verses.en: You walked through the sea;[NOTE:1] you passed through the surging waters,[NOTE:2] but left no footprints.[NOTE:3]
notes: The prefixed verbal form may be taken as a preterite or as an imperfect with past progressive force.sn Verses 16-18 depict the Lord coming in the storm to battle his enemies and subdue the sea. There is no record of such a storm in the historical account of the Red Sea crossing. The language the psalmist uses here is stereotypical and originates in Canaanite myth, where the storm god Baal subdues the sea in his quest for kingship. The psalmist has employed the stereotypical imagery to portray the exodus vividly and at the same time affirm that it is not Baal who subdues the sea, but Yahweh.
Heb “in the sea [was] your way.”
Heb “and your paths [were] in the mighty waters.”

verses.zh: 你 曾 藉 摩 西 和 亞 倫 的 手 引 導 你 的 百 姓 ， 好 像 羊 群 一 般 。
verses.en: You led your people like a flock of sheep,by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
